<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <meta name="color-scheme" content="light">
  <title>Black circle</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      background: #fff;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
      overflow: visible;
    }
    @media (forced-colors: active) {
      circle { fill: CanvasText; }
    }
  </style>
  <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 2 2'%3E%3Ccircle cx='1' cy='1' r='1'/%3E%3C/svg%3E">
</head>
<body>
  <main>
    <svg width="400" height="400" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="circle-title">
      <title id="circle-title">Black circle</title>
      <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200" fill="#000"/>
    </svg>
  </main>
</body>
</html>

content.text:
I didn't change `0.html` because I couldn't find anything to fix. It's a page that shows a black circle in the middle of the screen, and it already handles the usual things well:

- **Accessibility:** screen readers announce the circle as an image called "Black circle".
- **High-contrast mode:** Windows high-contrast mode recolours the circle so it stays visible.
- **Layout:** it stays centred and shrinks to fit small screens, including mobile browsers where the address bar changes the screen height.
- **Setup:** it has a proper character set, language and mobile viewport, and a matching circle favicon (the browser-tab icon).

There are two tiny tidy-ups, but neither changes how the page looks:
- `overflow: visible` on the `svg` does nothing here, because the circle fits exactly inside its box.
- `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light">` could become `light dark` with a dark background option, if you want the page to follow the system's dark mode.

What kind of improvement did you have in mind? For example: dark-mode support, animation, making it smaller, or changing the look.
